newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance seeks offers for Lyndon.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance seeks offers for Lyndon.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co said Tuesday it has hired Salomon Brothers to seek offers for the sale of Mercury's Lyndon Insurance Group, headquartered in St. Louis.

Mercury said Salomon, which it previously engaged to advise it on financial matters, is in discussions with several parties that have expressed an interest in purchasing Lyndon. The names of the parties were not disclosed.

"It is appropriate for Mercury to take a serious look at these expressions of interest," William Brandt Jr., Mercury president and chief executive officer, said in a statement. "We cannot predict the outcome of the discussions, but we are prepared to make a decision and act promptly within regulatory guidelines."
Mercury said it is working closely with the Missouri insurance commissioner in connection with the sale efforts.

Lyndon has been managed as a stand-alone operation. Its divestiture would have no effect on Mercury's ability to operate its core consumer finance business and to continue offering add-on insurance products to its consumer finance customers, the company said.
Lyndon was acquired by Mercury in October 1995 for $72.5 million. Subsequently, other smaller insurance operations of Mercury were merged with Lyndon, the company said.
